You will compare one known error in a data agent's work against a ranked list of items produced by a reviewer. Your job is to decide whether any item in the list identifies this known error, and if so, which one.

An item identifies the known error only if both of these hold:
- It is about the same thing: the same table, and the same column, computation, filter, or join.
- It points to the same problem: what the item says is wrong, assumed, or missing is the same as what went wrong in the known error. It does not matter whether the item is phrased as an assumption the agent made ("the agent assumes ...") or as a problem in the work ("this does not match ..."); judge by meaning.

An item does not count if it only says that something may be wrong without saying what, such as "this column may be computed incorrectly". An item about the same column but a different problem does not count.

If more than one item identifies the error, report the highest-ranked one. If you are unsure, say so rather than guessing.

Return a JSON object with:
- "verdict": "match", "no_match", or "unsure".
- "rank": the position of the matching item (1 is the top), or null.
- "quote": the exact words from the matching item that show it identifies the error, or null.
- "reason": one short sentence.

=== Known error ===
Table: int_ad_reporting__unified_campaign_metrics
What the agent's work assumed: Google 的 ROAS 在计算中先四舍五入到 4 位小数也没关系
What was actually required or true: ROAS 不做舍入

=== Reviewer's ranked list for this table ===
[
  {
    "rank": 1,
    "item": {
      "statement": "The unified campaign metrics model can be populated from its first configured source alone, without appending Google Ads, Facebook Ads, or LinkedIn records.",
      "about": "requirement",
      "target": "intermediate.int_ad_reporting__unified_campaign_metrics",
      "evidence_of_dependence": "src=srcs[0]; return 'SELECT\\n'+',\\n'.join(selections)+f'\\nFROM {src}'",
      "alternative": "The contract requires: \"Combine four platform feeds into a standardized base\" and lists Amazon, Google, Facebook, and LinkedIn.",
      "reason": "This determines whether three entire platform populations are included.",
      "updates": null,
      "id": "c4-1",
      "call": 4
    }
  },
  {
    "rank": 2,
    "item": {
      "statement": "The unified campaign metrics source already exposes the output metric names or the generator's generic aliases, so platform-specific metric mapping is unnecessary.",
      "about": "data",
      "target": "intermediate.int_ad_reporting__unified_campaign_metrics",
      "evidence_of_dependence": "aliases includes 'impressions':'total_impressions' and 'conversions':'total_conversions'; otherwise srcname=aliases.get(out,out).",
      "alternative": "The contract explicitly maps Amazon \"revenue_7d from sales_7_d\", \"revenue_30d from sales_30_d\", \"conversions from purchases_30_d\", and \"daily_budget from campaign_budget_amount\".",
      "reason": "These mappings affect core revenue, conversion, budget, and volume fields and may prevent the query from binding.",
      "updates": null,
      "id": "c4-4",
      "call": 4
    }
  },
  {
    "rank": 3,
    "item": {
      "statement": "The LinkedIn staging campaign report exposes a conversions column and is equivalent to the specified raw feed for USD cost, conversion values, dates, and source-level filtering.",
      "about": "data",
      "target": "intermediate.int_ad_reporting__unified_campaign_metrics.linkedin_rows",
      "evidence_of_dependence": "FROM staging.stg_linkedin_ads__campaign_report; CAST(COALESCE(conversions, 0) AS DECIMAL(12,2)) AS conversions",
      "alternative": "The contract specifies raw.linkedin_ad_analytics_by_campaign_data, with conversions from \"conversion_value_in_local_currency cast to integer\" and filtering on cost_in_usd; the documented LinkedIn staging schema has no conversions column.",
      "reason": "The substituted source can prevent binding and does not establish the required monetary and conversion mappings.",
      "updates": null,
      "id": "c11-1",
      "call": 11
    }
  },
  {
    "rank": 4,
    "item": {
      "statement": "Performance tiers, campaign age, lifecycle stage, and quality flags for unified campaign metrics are already available as upstream columns and need no derivation.",
      "about": "data",
      "target": "intermediate.int_ad_reporting__unified_campaign_metrics",
      "evidence_of_dependence": "spec=special.get(name,{}); srcname=aliases.get(out,out); expr=f'CASE WHEN {srcname} IS NULL THEN NULL ELSE TRY_CAST({srcname} AS {t}) END'",
      "alternative": "The contract requires platform-specific tier thresholds and \"campaign_age_days: days since the earliest observed date_day ... in the full base\", followed by lifecycle and quality computations.",
      "reason": "The generic projection depends on fields that the specification instead requires this model to compute.",
      "updates": null,
      "id": "c4-3",
      "call": 4
    }
  },
  {
    "rank": 5,
    "item": {
      "statement": "The unified campaign metrics model does not require source-level quality filters, a rolling 365-day date filter, positive-impression screening, or exclusion of flagged quality issues.",
      "about": "requirement",
      "target": "intermediate.int_ad_reporting__unified_campaign_metrics",
      "evidence_of_dependence": "The generic query ends with f'\\nFROM {src}' and adds no WHERE clause.",
      "alternative": "The contract says \"Keep rows where date_day is within the last 365 days\", \"Keep rows where impressions>0\", and \"Exclude rows flagged with has_data_quality_issues\", in addition to source-specific filters.",
      "reason": "These omitted filters define the eligible output population.",
      "updates": null,
      "id": "c4-2",
      "call": 4
    }
  },
  {
    "rank": 6,
    "item": {
      "statement": "Execution timestamps and source freshness timestamps for unified campaign metrics can be read directly from identically named upstream fields.",
      "about": "data",
      "target": "intermediate.int_ad_reporting__unified_campaign_metrics",
      "evidence_of_dependence": "Unmapped output columns use srcname=aliases.get(out,out) and TRY_CAST({srcname} AS {t}).",
      "alternative": "The contract maps Amazon \"source_updated_at from _dbt_loaded_at\" and requires \"processed_at set to the execution timestamp\".",
      "reason": "The required audit fields have explicit sourcing rules that the generic projection does not implement.",
      "updates": null,
      "id": "c4-5",
      "call": 4
    }
  },
  {
    "rank": 7,
    "item": {
      "statement": "The generic CTR tier thresholds should apply to Google and Facebook rows that do not meet their platform-specific MEDIUM thresholds.",
      "about": "requirement",
      "target": "intermediate.int_ad_reporting__unified_campaign_metrics.ctr_performance_tier",
      "evidence_of_dependence": "WHEN platform = 'facebook_ads' AND click_through_rate >= 0.9 THEN 'MEDIUM' WHEN click_through_rate >= 1.0 THEN 'HIGH' WHEN click_through_rate >= 0.5 THEN 'MEDIUM'",
      "alternative": "The contract assigns Google \"MEDIUM when ≥0.8; else LOW\" and Facebook \"MEDIUM when ≥0.9; else LOW\", reserving generic thresholds for \"others\".",
      "reason": "The fallback upgrades low-performing Google and Facebook rows into MEDIUM.",
      "updates": null,
      "id": "c11-2",
      "call": 11
    }
  },
  {
    "rank": 8,
    "item": {
      "statement": "For every otherwise eligible base row, the data-quality predicate evaluates to TRUE or FALSE rather than NULL.",
      "about": "data",
      "target": "intermediate.int_ad_reporting__unified_campaign_metrics.has_data_quality_issues",
      "evidence_of_dependence": "clicks > impressions OR cost < 0 OR click_through_rate > 100 OR cost_per_click > 50 AS has_data_quality_issues ... AND NOT has_data_quality_issues",
      "alternative": "The contract requires \"TRUE when clicks>impressions or cost<0 or CTR>100 or CPC>50; otherwise FALSE\"; a CASE expression with ELSE FALSE would retain rows whose comparisons are unknown but none are true.",
      "reason": "Nullable KPI values can make the predicate NULL and silently exclude rows not affirmatively flagged by the documented rules.",
      "updates": null,
      "id": "c15-1",
      "call": 15
    }
  },
  {
    "rank": 9,
    "item": {
      "statement": "A lower date bound alone implements the rolling last-365-days output window because future-dated rows cannot reach this model.",
      "about": "data",
      "target": "intermediate.int_ad_reporting__unified_campaign_metrics final date filter",
      "evidence_of_dependence": "WHERE date_day >= CURRENT_DATE - INTERVAL '365 days'",
      "alternative": "The contract requires dates \"within the last 365 days relative to execution\"; the new query supplies no upper bound.",
      "reason": "Most previously omitted filters are now implemented, but future dates would still be retained if present upstream.",
      "updates": "c4-2",
      "id": "c11-4",
      "call": 11
    }
  },
  {
    "rank": 10,
    "item": {
      "statement": "Unparseable LinkedIn numeric values may be treated as zero rather than rejected or distinguished from missing values.",
      "about": "requirement",
      "target": "intermediate.int_ad_reporting__unified_campaign_metrics.linkedin_rows",
      "evidence_of_dependence": "COALESCE(TRY_CAST(conversion_value_in_local_currency AS INTEGER), 0) and WHERE COALESCE(TRY_CAST(cost_in_usd AS DOUBLE), 0) >= 0",
      "alternative": "The contract requires numeric casts and defaults but does not explicitly authorize treating failed conversions as zero; it says to keep rows where \"cost_in_usd is non-negative\".",
      "reason": "Malformed values can become legitimate-looking zero metrics and pass the source filter.",
      "updates": null,
      "id": "c20-2",
      "call": 20
    }
  }
]
